page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr9ae.48xlarge is a bare-metal compute instance belonging to the ECS Bare Metal family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 9T95 processors clocked at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz. The configuration provides 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1536.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a balanced 8.0 GB of memory per core. The host runs on a KVM hypervisor infrastructure, offering direct access to underlying execution capabilities without shared-tenant CPU contention.

In terms of I/O connectivity, the instance is provisioned with 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, accommodating large data transfers and low-latency inter-node communication. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, meaning external network storage must be attached for persistent state management. Operating without local NVMe drives places full dependency on network-attached storage architectures, where the 100 Gbps network capacity becomes essential for sustained storage bandwidth and high-throughput pipeline execution.

From a hardware efficiency perspective, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio positions the instance in the memory-optimized tier, minimizing compute waste for memory-heavy processes that do not mandate graphic accelerators. The large memory capacity combined with 192 dedicated physical threads makes this server fit for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed data analytics engines, heavy enterprise resource planning platforms, and consolidated multi-tenant container virtualization environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr9ae.48xlarge is an ECS Bare Metal server engineered for memory-intensive enterprise computing. Powered by dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T95 processors operating at 2.25 GHz across 192 vCPUs, the instance supplies 1536.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. High-throughput data ingestion and low-latency node communications are supported by a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth configuration. The server includes no integrated GPUs and possesses zero bundled local storage, requiring persistent data to reside on external cloud storage volumes. With substantial core parallelism, large memory capacity, and dedicated bare-metal hypervisor management, this configuration exhibits high resource density for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale distributed analytics, extensive enterprise resource planning platforms, and memory-heavy container virtualization clusters.
